newsitem.title: USA: Rockford Park District, Ill., rated A1 by Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Rockford Park District, Ill., rated A1 by Moody's.

text.p: MOODY'S RATES ROCKFORD PARK DISTRICT, IL
Rockford Park District, IL
County
Illinois
Moody's Rating
General Obligation Limited Tax Bonds, Series 1997
Rating A1
Sale Amount $5,050,000.00
Expected Sale Date 07/08/97
Rating Description General Obligation, Limited Tax

NEW YORK, July 2, 1997 -- Moody's Investors Service has assigned an A1 rating and stable outlook to the district's general obligation limited tax bonds in recognition of a trend of favorable financial performance, with support from a growing property tax base and increasing fee derived revenue. Reduced local area unemployment rates are noted, although the manufacturing based economy remains susceptible to economic downturn. Recently adopted property tax cap limitations in Winnebago County are not expected to have an adverse effect on operations in the near-term. These factors are discussed more fully below:

Maintenance of sizable reserves in the Corporate and Recreations Funds, as well as the ability to adjust fees and programs provides significant flexibility. Surpluses generated by golf course and water theme park operations support general obligation debt issued for their development, as well as other capital needs. Although property taxes continue to represent the primary district revenue source, dependence has been reduced as fee revenues have increased. This factor is important since Winnebago County voters authorized property tax cap limitations in the November 1996 election. While this limitation on property levy growth may have an adverse effect on operations over time, continuing tax base and fee-based revenue growth are offsetting factors in the near-term.

Debt levels, while moderate, are mainly attributable to overlapping jurisdictions. More than one-quarter of the district's outstanding debt is in the form of alternate bonds supported by pledged theme park, golf course and ice skating rink revenues, with the associated property tax levy abated. An additional one-eighth of bonded debt is in the form of alternate bonds supported by annual non-referendum borrowing to meet debt service requirements. Future borrowing reflects these annual rollover issues, plus yearly borrowing in the range of $3 million to meet maintenance requirements. Approximately $2.05 million of the current offering will be applied to alternate bond repayment.

While alternate bond structures may have timing issues related to the property tax abatement, and the sufficiency of funds to make debt service payments, the district has covenanted in bond ordinances for all its alternate bond series that prior to property tax levy abatement the necessary offsetting cash will be on hand. Also favorable is positive performance of the district's enterprise operations.

Taxable valuation continues to grow at a steady pace. Recent building permit data indicates continuation of this trend. However, the local economy remains centered in durable goods manufacturing. While unemployment rates have exhibited improvement in recent years, there has been a general upward movement during recessionary periods.

The district's unlimited tax general obligation bonds are rated A1. The absence of a rating distinction reflects the dedicated debt service levy that secures limited tax bonds. This levy, commonly referred to as the debt service extension base, is equivalent to the district's 1996 levy for non-referendum bonds. While the amount of taxes that may be levied is limited, there is no limitation as to rate. ANALYSTS:
Harvey Zachem, Analyst, Public Finance Group, Moody's Investors Service
Steven Levine, Senior Credit Officer, Public Finance Group, Moody's Investors Service
